title: For Trump, the Iran War Is Stuck Between Combat and Genuine Peace
partialText: The war has deteriorated over the past six months into Mr. Trump’s own version of a “forever war,” with no clear goals and no end in sight.

title: These Tanks Can Hold 90 Million Barrels of Oil. They Have Just 22 Million.
partialText: Oil companies and governments are consuming their once vast stockpiles as Iran and the United States continue to struggle for control over the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Nepali Flood Survivors Face Profound Loss, Pressing Needs and Murky Futures
partialText: The disaster has left countless people with little or nothing of the lives they had built, struggling with immediate survival and unsure how to rebuild.

title: Nepal Roughly Doubles Number of Missing After Flood
partialText: Also, Trump orders the creation of a space academy. Here’s the latest at the end of Friday.

title: Milo Yiannopoulos, a Right-Wing Provocateur, Is Arrested by ICE
partialText: Mr. Yiannopoulos, a prominent early supporter of President Trump, was detained at the New Orleans airport. The Trump administration publicized his arrest and shared a mug shot.

title: Trump Administration Looks to Give a Swath of Yosemite Park to Developer
partialText: The proposed land swap would allow easy access to the crown jewel of the national park system. Democrats and former Park Service officials are incensed.

title: You Can Photograph This Pretty Irish Castle. You Just Can’t Go In.
partialText: Tourists still flock to the picturesque 16th-century Dunguaire Castle on Galway Bay. But in recent years, a dispute over ownership has prevented visitors from entering.

title: Social Media and the Myth of the Big Tobacco Moment
partialText: Smoking used to be everywhere, the way Facebook, TikTok, Snap, YouTube and Instagram are now. Society decided to break the habit, but it took a long time.

title: Why Countries Are Pushing Social Media Bans Despite Their Flaws
partialText: Proposals for curbing social media use among children have wide support, but critics say they are ineffective.

title: Unstable Manhattan Building Had More Damaged Columns Than Previously Known
partialText: Drawings obtained by The New York Times and reviewed by engineers show insufficient reinforcements on eight more steel columns than previously known at a Manhattan building.

title: Why Putin Is Fighting On, Even as His Problems Multiply
partialText: There is little sign that public exhaustion, economic headwinds or increased Ukrainian strikes are changing the Russian leader’s view that he will eventually achieve victory.

title: Critics Blast Metropolitan Museum’s Plan to Honor John Galliano
partialText: Galliano, a fashion industry giant championed by Anna Wintour, was found guilty of a hate crime for his antisemitic outbursts in 2011.

title: Sun-Ways Is Testing Out Train Track Solar Farms
partialText: A pilot program placing solar panels between the rails has proven successful enough that the idea is spreading to Italy, France and Korea.

title: She Filmed the Towers That Morning. 25 Years Later, She Finally Watched.
partialText: A young college graduate filmed the World Trade Center attack from the fire escape of her Chinatown apartment. For many years, she avoided looking at the footage.

title: Judge Throws Out Key 9/11 Confession as Tainted by Torture
partialText: Prosecutors argued the statements by the defendant, Khalid Shaikh Mohammed, were crucial evidence for the eventual death-penalty trial.

title: How the Foo Fighters Fill a Three-Hour Set List, Night After Night
partialText: Dave Grohl, the frontman of the Foo Fighters, tells us how he packs 31 years into 3 hours with something for fans of every generation.

title: ‘Trump Voters Are Finally Starting to Sour on Him’
partialText: Democrats want fighters. A former Republican has ideas.

title: This Is Looting by Another Name
partialText: Our cultural heritage is being sold off for parts.

title: China Sees Opportunity in America’s Recent A.I. Security Scares
partialText: A leading Chinese A.I. start-up released its latest model and made the case that China’s embrace of open software is safer than Silicon Valley’s closed approach.
